principle: One observation = one country/indicator pair. No value enters without its explicit denominator, its confidence level and the reasoning that produced it.

confidence.sourced: Figure published by an identified, citable source (annual report, statistical body, study).
confidence.declared: Figure given directly by a professional or an organisation in the country, unpublished.
confidence.estimated: Estimate produced by reasoning, with no source. Never to be quoted outside this repository.

status.disputed: Value whose method has been called into question. See the reasoning field.
status.verified: Value confronted with a source and confirmed.

rules: The denominator is settled BEFORE collection. Comparing French self-declared performers with Croatian salaried ones is not a comparison.
Always prefer the median to the mean for indicators about the trade: the distributions are bimodal.
An estimated value is never quoted outside this repository, not in a meeting, not in an application.
A fee is not a performance. Rehearsals, residencies, workshops and outreach all generate fees with no show.
A change of value goes through its own commit, with the reasoning in the message.

indicators.label: Structuring venues
indicators.denominator: Permanent unit of puppetry with a venue of its own and the backing of a public authority (state, Land, canton, region, municipality), charged with presenting or creating work. A named puppet stage or ensemble counts whether or not it holds its own legal personality. A museum that programmes shows is not a venue of diffusion and creation and does not count, whatever the quality of what it programmes; a theatre that also keeps a museum does. Excludes funded companies without a venue, festivals, and programming strands or occasional co-productions.
indicators.ruling: Settled 2026-07-27, after Czechia, Hungary and Croatia all stalled on the same question and the earlier wording — 'permanent organisation with a building of its own' — turned out to be counting company law rather than puppetry. Three findings decided it. First, output: in Czechia the integrated stages are the same size as the freestanding houses, Most playing 276 puppet performances against Alfa's 248, so the distinction separates nothing that matters. Second, applicability: the obvious alternative, a majority-of-repertoire test, needs a performance count per venue, and of the ten countries collected only Czechia and Croatia publish any puppetry figure at all — a rule decidable in a fifth of the field is not a rule. Third, and decisively, internal consistency: performances counted by form already includes puppetry made inside drama houses, so excluding those houses from venues assigns their output to no venue at all and breaks every ratio built from the two columns. In Czechia that is 479 performances belonging nowhere. The old wording also failed a practical test: its own author applied it wrongly within a day, counting Czechia at 8 by missing that Divadlo Lampion sits inside Divadla Kladno. A criterion that cannot be applied twice the same way is not a criterion.
indicators.backing: Since 2026-07-27 this indicator, like schools, requires the named list of the venues composing it, in the 'venues_list' field. The build fails when the number of entries does not equal 'lower_bound', and when the kinds declared in the entries do not match the 'units' object. A count that cannot be enumerated cannot be audited: before this field existed the names and addresses collected sat in the reasoning as prose, unreadable by any program and absent from the map. The one exemption is a count taken from a statistical aggregate that names no establishment, which carries its total under 'units.unknown' and no list.
indicators.unit_of_count: The permanent puppetry unit. Every observation researched at source carries a 'units' object splitting the count into 'house' — a freestanding organisation whose vocation is puppetry — and 'stage' — a named puppet stage or ensemble inside a larger organisation. Where the source is a statistical aggregate that names no establishments, the split is unknowable and goes under 'unknown'. The three keys sum to the count. This keeps the strict organisation-only reading recoverable for ever: it is the 'house' figure, and nobody has to take the ruling on trust.
indicators.known_bias: Mechanically understates systems where vitality runs through companies: Italy, Spain, the Netherlands. The ruling of 2026-07-27 removed a second bias running the other way, and it is worth naming because it flattered exactly the countries this map is about: counting legal persons rewarded systems whose puppetry was organised into separate institutions, the socialist state-theatre legacy above all, and penalised those where it lives inside larger houses. Expect counts to rise in the west as Germany's Sparten and France's labelled structures are read under the new wording, and expect the east-west gap to narrow. That narrowing is a correction, not a distortion.

indicators.label: National schools
indicators.denominator: Higher education course in puppetry or object theatre arts whose award is recognised by the State. Puppetry or object theatre must be a named specialism of the course, not a subject taught inside a broader curriculum.
indicators.ownership: Not a criterion. Public, private and foundation-run institutions are treated alike: what is asked of the establishment is that the qualification it awards be state-recognised, not that the State own the walls. Settled 2026-07-27, after the Hungarian case, where a national theatre university transferred to a private foundation in 2020 was blocking the count.
indicators.scope: European establishments only. A course meeting every other criterion but sitting outside Europe does not enter the count, which is what excludes Anadolu Üniversitesi in Eskişehir from Turkey's. This scope is deliberately narrower than population_M, which since the ruling of 2026-07-27 counts transcontinental countries entire: see that indicator's known_bias for what the mismatch does to any ratio built from the two.
indicators.object_theatre: Counts. A specialism in object theatre, figure theatre or material theatre enters the indicator on the same footing as one whose title carries the word puppet. Settled 2026-07-27, after the Latvian case, where a four-year specialism built with the national puppet theatre was excluded on the sole ground that no course title used the word. The naming of the field varies by country and is not evidence about what is taught.
indicators.known_bias: Courses open and close with each intake. Prefer the annual flow of graduates in the long run.
indicators.unit_of_count: The establishment, never the programme. An academy carrying one bachelor's and three master's degrees in puppetry counts 1.
indicators.backing: Requires the named list of the establishments composing it, in the 'establishments' field. The build fails when the number of establishments with 'counted': true does not equal 'lower_bound': a count must be justified one at a time. This was the only indicator carrying such a list until 2026-07-27, when venues was given one too, on the same argument.

indicators.label: Population
indicators.denominator: Total population of the country, its whole territory included. Transcontinental countries are counted entire.
indicators.ruling: Settled 2026-07-27, replacing an earlier denominator that asked for the European part alone of Russia and Turkey. Splitting a country along a continental line cost more precision than it bought: the figures involved are not precise enough to carry the distinction, and building Eastern Thrace out of provincial tables, or European Russia out of federal districts, meant constructing a number rather than reading one.
indicators.known_bias: The scope of this indicator no longer matches the scope of schools, and that is deliberate rather than an oversight. Population covers the whole country; schools counts only establishments in Europe. Any ratio built from the two is therefore inconsistent for Russia and Turkey. For Turkey the effect is nil, its schools count being zero under either scope. For Russia it inflates the denominator, the counted school being in Saint Petersburg while the population now includes Siberia and the Far East. Read per-inhabitant figures for those two countries with that in mind, or exclude them.

indicators.label: Performances per year
indicators.denominator: Performances of puppetry or object theatre given in the country during the reference year, tour dates and dates played abroad included. What is wanted is the form, whoever produces it.
indicators.basis: Mandatory field on every observation, and the reason this indicator is not comparable with itself across all countries. Two values. 'form' means the source counts performances by genre of production, so a puppetry production staged by a drama theatre is inside and a puppet theatre's straight play is outside — this is the denominator above, met exactly. 'organisation' means the source counts the output of named puppet theatres whatever they staged, which is a proxy: it drops puppetry made elsewhere and picks up non-puppetry made in the right building. The build refuses an observation that does not say which it is.
indicators.ruling: Settled 2026-07-27, after Estonia and Latvia disagreed on the first day of collection. The first denominator written that morning was organisation-based, on the assumption that statistical offices count institutions. Estonia refutes it: its table KU091 classes every performance in the country by genre and carries 'nuku- ja objektiteatri lavastus' as its own category. Latvia confirms it: its table KUT020 lists state culture companies by name, and puppetry is whatever the Latvian Puppet Theatre did. Rather than force one country into the other's shape, the target denominator is the one worth having — the form — and each observation declares how far its source falls from it.
indicators.known_bias: On an 'organisation' basis, measures the institutional segment and only it. Independent companies reporting to nobody are absent, which understates exactly the systems the venues indicator already understates — the same mechanism twice, so the two errors compound rather than cancel. A 'form' basis escapes that only as far as its statistical office reaches, which is usually to the theatres that file returns and no further. And the class travels badly: a country whose statistics isolate no puppetry produces no value here at all, which is a fact about the statistical apparatus and not about the activity. Never read a missing value as a low one. One further warning, for the by_venue lists: these are institutional data and the rule of this repository applies to them in full. A house playing 573 performances to school groups is not thereby better than one playing 248 on international tour. The lists exist to show a distribution and to be contradicted, not to rank anybody.
indicators.no_value: A country whose statistics do not isolate puppetry carries no observation for this indicator at all, rather than a zero or an estimate. The build treats the indicator as optional for that reason: it is the first indicator in the series a country is allowed not to have. This is deliberate — the alternative was an estimate, and an estimate here would be indistinguishable from a measurement of a small country.
indicators.by_venue: Optional named list of the producers behind the count, with what each played. A national total is a sum, and a sum hides its own distribution: 7 596 Czech performances says nothing about whether ten houses play 760 each or three play most of it. The list also makes the figure far more refutable — a total can only be checked by reopening one table, while a named producer can be contradicted by anyone who knows that theatre. It is deliberately NOT a field on the venue record. The two are different populations: 33 Czech theatres played puppetry and 10 of them are counted as venues, so hanging the figures on venue records would make the other 23 producers vanish and make every unlisted venue look idle. Each entry carries 'venue', the name in venues_list it corresponds to, or null when the producer is not a counted venue. Each entry declares its own 'unit', because sources do not agree on what they count: Czechia publishes performances, Germany publishes productions. 'by_venue_covers' is mandatory alongside the list and states in words what fraction of the headline the parts represent. The build refuses a list of performances summing above the headline. Where units differ from the headline no sum check is possible, and the covers note has to say so.

indicators.label: Performances per performer per year
indicators.denominator: TO BE SETTLED. Three incompatible options: (a) anyone declaring themselves a professional puppeteer, (b) anyone who performed at least once in the year, (c) any performer on a permanent contract or equivalent. The option chosen changes the result by a factor of two to three.
indicators.known_bias: Identified trap: counting fees instead of performances. In France the threshold for unemployment insurance can be reached without ever getting behind a booth.

indicators.label: Active repertoire titles per performer
indicators.denominator: Titles a performer actually played at least once during the year.
indicators.known_bias: Separates an economy of stock from an economy of flow. Probably the most discriminating indicator in the series.

indicators.label: Life of a production
indicators.denominator: Performances accumulated over the whole exploitation of a production, until it is retired.
indicators.known_bias: Requires several years of hindsight. On recent productions the value is truncated.

indicators.label: Share performing fewer than 20 dates a year
indicators.denominator: Same population as the dates indicator. Depends on the same ruling.
indicators.known_bias: The most fragile indicator in the series: the population that does not perform is measured by nobody.

indicators.label: Young-audience share
indicators.denominator: Share of performances played to audiences of children, in and out of school alike.
indicators.known_bias: A very high share is not a virtue: it can signal the absence of an adult market.

indicators.label: Share of income from performing
indicators.denominator: Share of annual artistic income coming from performances, the remainder coming from workshops, teaching and unemployment insurance.
indicators.known_bias: Assumes analytical accounting that few professionals keep. To be collected by declarative survey.

establishment.purpose: Named record of a school, carried by the 'schools' observation. It makes the count auditable and places the points on the map. A country with zero schools can still carry establishments: those are the candidates examined and set aside, and they are often the most useful information in the record.

fields.name: Name of the establishment in its own language; Latin transcription accepted.
fields.city: The city where the teaching actually happens, not the administrative seat when the two differ.
fields.address: Postal address read at source. null when not verified, never reconstructed from memory.
fields.lat: Latitude in decimal degrees, locality level. Makes no claim to locate a street.
fields.lon: Longitude in decimal degrees, same caveat.
fields.status: public, private, or foundation. Descriptive only: since the ruling of 2026-07-27 it carries no weight in the count. 'foundation' covers institutions transferred from the state to a foundation, as in Hungary: neither quite public nor private.
fields.award: Name and level of the qualification granted, or the precise reason when the establishment is set aside.
fields.description: Two or three sentences in English: what the school is, since when, and what makes its position in the count what it is. Mandatory, the build refuses an empty description.
fields.counted: true when the establishment enters the indicator. The number of true values equals lower_bound.
fields.exclusion_reason: Mandatory when counted is false. Values: closed, not_degree_granting, outside_scope, outside_denominator, unconfirmed. 'not_degree_granting' means the establishment awards no state-recognised qualification, whoever owns it. 'outside_denominator' means it awards one, but not in puppetry or object theatre. The value 'private' was withdrawn on 2026-07-27: private ownership stopped being a ground for exclusion, and every establishment carrying it was re-examined on the award instead.
fields.source: URL actually opened and read. Mandatory as soon as counted is true.
fields.checked_on: ISO date of the check. A record without a date cannot be reused.

establishment.projection: Coordinates are converted into the SVG frame by tools/projection.py, fitted on the outlines of the base map. The build refuses a point that falls outside its own country outline, and reports those it had to pull inland, the coastline of the base map being generalised.

venue.purpose: Named record of a puppetry venue, carried by the 'venues' observation. Same role as 'establishment' does for schools: it makes the count auditable one entry at a time and puts the point on the map.

fields.name: Name of the venue in its own language; Latin transcription accepted.
fields.city: The city where the venue actually plays.
fields.address: Postal address read at source. null when not verified, never reconstructed from memory.
fields.lat: Latitude in decimal degrees. Read from a gazetteer, not deduced from an address.
fields.lon: Longitude in decimal degrees, same caveat.
fields.unit: 'house' for a freestanding organisation whose vocation is puppetry, 'stage' for a named puppet stage or ensemble inside a larger organisation. The tally must match the observation's 'units' object.
fields.parent: For a stage, the organisation it sits inside. null for a house.
fields.authority: The public body behind it — ministry, region, county, municipality — as read, not as assumed. null when the source names none, which is itself worth seeing.
fields.registration: Register number or legal identifier where the source gives one: an IČO, an Očevidnik number, a founding decree. What makes the entry re-findable by someone who doubts it.
fields.source: URL actually opened and read. Mandatory.

venue.geocoding: Coordinates come from the OpenStreetMap Nominatim gazetteer, queried on the address where one was read and on the venue name and city otherwise, and the query is recorded. A coordinate is never computed from an address by hand. The build validates by containment, as it does for schools: a point falling outside its own country outline is refused, and the coordinate is wrong rather than the tolerance being too tight.
